extraction_scope: Worker-6 source-reviewed mechanism/phenotype ontology claims from XML sections, tables, figure captions, PDF page 12 render, and linked database rows.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The three cyclic dipeptides have direct antibacterial activity against the wound-associated bacterial panel in MIC/MBC and inhibition-zone assays.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Recorded as phenotype activity; no molecular killing mechanism is inferred from MIC/MBC or zone data alone.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Checkerboard assays show mostly synergistic CDP + ampicillin interactions, with additive outcomes preserved where the source table reports them.

source_locator.locator: xml:table=4; xml:sec=Cyclic dipeptides synergistically enhance the activity of ampicillin against wound pathogens

mechanism_claims.limitations: The claim is limited to in vitro checkerboard interaction against the tested panel and does not establish a shared molecular target.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CDP 1, CDP 2, CDP 3 with and without ampicillin
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Figure 4 and source text support inhibition of bacterial biofilm formation, with stronger inhibition for CDP + ampicillin combinations and CDP 3 combinations.

source_locator.locator: xml:fig=4; pdf:page=12:Figure 4; xml:sec=Combination of cyclic dipeptides and ampicillin significantly increases the inhibition of biofilms formation

mechanism_claims.limitations: Exact percent inhibition values are not tabulated in local source text; database exact values are preserved as source_conflict rather than promoted to source_verified.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CDP 1, CDP 2, CDP 3 in human peripheral blood mononuclear cells
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Source text reports increased IL-10 and IL-4 production and no significant pro-inflammatory cytokine increase under tested conditions.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Immunomodulatory actions of cyclic dipeptides; xml:fig=5; pdf:page=12:Figure 5

mechanism_claims.limitations: Recorded as host-cell cytokine response; figure caption/text cytokine naming is preserved without expanding to a therapeutic mechanism.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CDP 1, CDP 2, CDP 3 against intracellular S. aureus in J774 macrophages
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Source text and Figure 6 report reduced intracellular S. aureus burden after CDP treatment at MIC-scaled concentrations.
direct_assay_types: J774 macrophage intracellular S. aureus assay

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Cyclic dipeptides recorded significant toxicity toward the intracellular S. aureus; xml:fig=6

mechanism_claims.limitations: The source describes intracellular bacterial burden reduction; exact plotted values are not normalized outside the figure.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: CDP 1, CDP 2, CDP 3 against FS, VERO, and L231 normal cell lines
mechanism_claims.claim_text: Source text reports no cytotoxicity against the tested normal cell lines over 5-100 μg/mL after 72 h.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=Cyclic dipeptides recorded no cytotoxicity toward normal cell lines; xml:fig=7

mechanism_claims.limitations: Recorded as tested-cell-line cytotoxicity evidence only; it is not generalized to in vivo safety.
